sections.html: Aphanius vladykovi reaches a maximum length of 5-6 cm and is one of the easier species of the genus to keep. The available strain is captive-bred, offered at 4-5 cm.
Members of the killifish genus Aphanius appear only in Europe, North Africa and Asia. Aphanius vladykovi inhabits only a small area in Iran; the exact collecting site of the strain is Boldaji.

This fish is kept best in groups in large tanks with a lot of plants, where the displays of the males can be enjoyed. Many Aphanius species need changing temperatures as in the wild and do not thrive well in indoor aquaria; some also need salt and full-strength sunlight, but A. vladykovi does not. Tolerance for water temperature is very high, from 12-32°C, so the fish can be kept in outdoor tanks in summer. Fish returned from outdoor tanks to the room aquarium most often show breathtaking colours and are very healthy.

In the aquarium hobby Aphanius are rarely seen. Many of the currently 22 accepted species and subspecies are in danger of extinction due to habitat destruction, which is why some specialised aquarists breed them as a conservation effort.

photos.caption: Choghakhor Wetland is a wetland in Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari Province, Iran, considered to be one of the most important sites in Iran for the endemic Zagros pupfish, Aphanius vladykovi.
